summary: Logs a user into the cloud backend with username and password, establishing the session the User node reflects.
description: Log In sends the current `username` and `password` (string values) to the cloud backend when `login` (Do, signal) is triggered. On success the returned session is stored in the browser (it persists across reloads), the app-wide user service switches to the logged-in user — which updates every User node and fires their Logged In signal — and `success` (signal) fires. On a bad login or network problem `error` (string value) is set with the message and `failure` (signal) fires; nothing about the current session changes.
whenToUse: The action node behind a login form. To read who is logged in, or to react to session changes, use the User node; to create an account use Sign Up (which also logs the new user in); to end the session use Log Out.

ports.login: Signal input (displayed 'Do'); performs the login after pending input updates, so username/password wired from inputs are current.
ports.success: Signal; fires once the session is established. Typical next step: navigate to the logged-in page.
ports.failure: Signal; fires on rejected credentials or request failure. Show `error` to the user.
ports.error: String value holding the backend's error message from the last failed attempt.

patterns: Text Input `text` → `username`/`password`, Button `onClick` → `login`, `success` → navigation: the standard login form.
`error` → a Text node's `text`: surface backend messages like 'Invalid username/password' directly.
antiPatterns: Driving logged-in UI from this node's `success` signal alone — state belongs to the User node's `authenticated` boolean, which also covers sessions restored on reload.
